qpdf.notes: Collected locally 2026-07-27 (pikepdf 10.9.1 = qpdf). Magic was identical across 18 round-tripped inputs; trailer keys are deliberately NOT recorded because qpdf INHERITS them from the source document (a LibreOffice original keeps its /DocChecksum), so they identify the input, not qpdf.

pdfium.notes: Collected locally 2026-07-27 (pypdfium2 5.11.0). Magic identical across 18 round-tripped inputs; trailer keys source-inherited, see qpdf. Distinct from chrome_skia (d3ebe9e1): Chrome's print-to-PDF writer is Skia, not PDFium.

pymupdf.notes: Collected locally 2026-07-27 (PyMuPDF 1.28.0). Magic identical across 18 round-tripped inputs. NOT the same magic as mupdf_online_converter (e2e3cfd3) — see that entry's caveat.

mupdf_online_converter.notes: The SIGNATURE is empirically collected and verified (iLovePDF + Smallpdf, 2026-07-25). The NAME is an inference that local collection on 2026-07-27 did NOT confirm: PyMuPDF 1.28 emits magic c2b5c2b6, not this entry's e2e3cfd3 (the classic Adobe binary comment, which many tools copy). Treat 'mupdf' here as a label for a shared online-converter signature class, not a proven backend.
